{"id": "11:41/q20", "question": "When did the ark embark and settle, and how long was the voyage?", "turns_on": "Different transmitted dates and voyage durations.", "positions": [{"id": "11:41/q20/p1", "position": "It embarked on 10 Rajab and settled or disembarked on 10 Muharram, ʿĀshūrāʾ, about six months later.", "reasons": "Qatāda, ʿIkrima and Ibn ʿAbbās give the dates; Qatāda adds fasting on arrival and, in Ibn Abī Ḥātim, dusk-to-dusk fasting during the voyage. Ibn Jurayj says Friday at ʿAyn Warda and landfall at Baqardā on al-Jūdī."}, {"id": "11:41/q20/p2", "position": "It embarked on 1 Rajab and reached al-Jūdī on ʿĀshūrāʾ.", "reasons": "A prophetic report cited by al-Qurṭubī says Noah fasted all Rajab and later fasted with his companions on landing; Abū Ḥayyān contrasts ʿIkrima's tenth-of-Rajab report."}, {"id": "11:41/q20/p3", "position": "The voyage lasted 150 days.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās's report also gives eighty men with families."}, {"id": "11:41/q20/p4", "position": "The ark remained on water for about a year.", "reasons": "Ibn Isḥāq's itinerary has it circle the raised House seven times, reach Yemen, and return to al-Jūdī."}]}
{"id": "11:41/q21", "question": "What route and mooring site do reports give the ark?", "turns_on": "The distinct itineraries and reported mooring places.", "positions": [{"id": "11:41/q21/p1", "position": "It went to Mecca, circled the Kaaba for forty days, then settled on Mount Jūdī.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās gives this sequence."}, {"id": "11:41/q21/p2", "position": "It rose from ʿAyn Warda, circled the raised Kaaba site seven times, and settled at Baqardā on al-Jūdī.", "reasons": "Ibn Jurayj specifies Friday 10 Rajab and ʿĀshūrāʾ landfall."}, {"id": "11:41/q21/p3", "position": "It circled the raised, un-flooded House seven times, went to Yemen, and returned to al-Jūdī.", "reasons": "Ibn Isḥāq's report implies about a year afloat."}, {"id": "11:41/q21/p4", "position": "It moored by Kufa's Kinda gate.", "reasons": "Razīn ibn Ḥubaysh says this explains why he prayed there on Fridays."}]}
{"id": "11:41/q22", "question": "What other events aboard or after the voyage are reported?", "turns_on": "Distinct narrative reports about the voyage and its aftermath.", "positions": [{"id": "11:41/q22/p1", "position": "Ham had intercourse with his wife aboard; Noah prayed for a change to his offspring's complexion.", "reasons": "Abū Ṣāliḥ connects this with the Sudanese."}, {"id": "11:41/q22/p2", "position": "Noah sent a raven that delayed at carrion, then a dove returned with signs of receding water.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās gives an olive leaf and mud on the dove's feet. Another story says Noah cursed the crow and blessed the dove's neck ring, red feet and descendants; al-Thaʿlabī adds a partridge that found greenery and stayed away."}, {"id": "11:41/q22/p3", "position": "Noah founded a village named Eighty below al-Jūdī, where eighty languages emerged.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās says Arabic was among them and Noah interpreted for the inhabitants."}, {"id": "11:41/q22/p4", "position": "Cats appeared when Noah rubbed a lion's tail after mice gnawed the ark's ropes.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās's report specifies two cats."}, {"id": "11:41/q22/p5", "position": "Pigs appeared when Noah rubbed an elephant's tail to remove filth.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jawzī reports two pigs that ate the filth."}, {"id": "11:41/q22/p6", "position": "A believing old woman was saved inside her house after Noah forgot to call her aboard.", "reasons": "Al-Burṣawī reports a spiritually disclosed identification of the site with Bursa's Great Mosque, and cites the Mathnawī on perfected people's distant perception."}]}
{"id": "11:41/q23", "question": "How were animals and plants carried aboard?", "turns_on": "The reported means of gathering and loading living things.", "positions": [{"id": "11:41/q23/p1", "position": "The ark's decks separated beasts, wild animals and birds, and humans.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās places beasts below, wild animals and birds on the middle deck, forty men and forty women above, and ants high enough to avoid trampling."}, {"id": "11:41/q23/p2", "position": "A wind brought pairs of every kind of animal to Noah.", "reasons": "Al-Zuhrī includes beasts, birds, and livestock."}, {"id": "11:41/q23/p3", "position": "Gabriel gathered and boarded each male and female animal.", "reasons": "Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad says Gabriel held the male in his right hand and female in his left."}, {"id": "11:41/q23/p4", "position": "The ark carried every kind of tree, including a date palm from Paradise.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī transmits this as a prophetic report."}]}
{"id": "11:41/q24", "question": "What reports explain animal features associated with the ark?", "turns_on": "Two distinct etiological reports.", "positions": [{"id": "11:41/q24/p1", "position": "A goat's crooked tail and exposed sex followed its resistance to Noah; Noah's touch covered the ewe's sex.", "reasons": "Zayd ibn Thābit gives the account."}, {"id": "11:41/q24/p2", "position": "A hoopoe's nape tuft marks where a male buried its mate that died aboard.", "reasons": "An unnamed scholar reported this to Isḥāq."}]}
{"id": "11:41/q25", "question": "To whom do “forgiving, merciful” apply?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "11:41/q25/p1", "position": "To the believers or people aboard the ark.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Qurṭubī explicitly identify the passengers; al-Nasafī says mercy delivered them, and Abū Ḥayyān says God covered their sins after faith and repentance."}]}
{"id": "11:41/q26", "question": "What forgiveness and mercy does the closing clause describe?", "turns_on": "Whether the clause emphasizes pardon for sins, unearned grace, or care sustaining the ship.", "positions": [{"id": "11:41/q26/p1", "position": "God forgives the passengers' former sins and mercifully saves them after repentance.", "reasons": "Al-Muqātil identifies rescue from punishment; Ibn Abī Ḥātim reports Saʿīd ibn Jubayr's former idolatry. Al-Ṭabarī says God no longer punishes repentant returners; Ibn ʿAṭiyya adds concealment of sins, and al-Biqāʿī adds honor."}, {"id": "11:41/q26/p2", "position": "Their rescue came through unearned divine grace rather than the merit of their faith or deeds.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī warns survivors against crediting their own knowledge; al-Burṣawī and al-Ālūsī identify a Sunni account of sheer grace. Iṣlāḥī says one cannot know a deed's weight and must trust divine mercy."}, {"id": "11:41/q26/p3", "position": "God's mercy protects the ark's course and mooring from failure and the passengers from drowning.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾ says the visible means work only through God's sustaining care and that the invocation rests on forgiveness and mercy."}]}
{"id": "11:41/q27", "question": "Why does Noah mention forgiveness and mercy at this point?", "turns_on": "Whether the clause explains salvation, balances the account of destruction, or is a direct rationale for the command.", "positions": [{"id": "11:41/q27/p1", "position": "The words explain rescue and reassure the passengers amid danger.", "reasons": "Al-Kashshāf says they could not be saved without these attributes; al-Rāzī warns against self-credit. Ibn ʿĀshūr says emphatic particles reassure and hint at promised rescue; al-Ālūsī supplies “invoke God and fear no drowning.”"}, {"id": "11:41/q27/p2", "position": "It follows destruction of unbelievers to balance divine vengeance with mercy.", "reasons": "Ibn Kathīr compares 7:167 and 13:6."}, {"id": "11:41/q27/p3", "position": "It signals that obedience brings mercy, as boarding brought rescue.", "reasons": "Al-Wāḥidī and al-Ṭabrisī make the analogy; al-Ālūsī reports an implied rationale, “obey so God may save you.”"}, {"id": "11:41/q27/p4", "position": "It directly gives the reason for the boarding command.", "reasons": "Some infer the passengers' eventual salvation from the clause; al-Ālūsī objects that a direct causal connection is absent unless an unstated rationale is supplied."}]}
{"id": "11:41/q28", "question": "What inward reading is given to the ark and divine name?", "turns_on": "Different inward identifications of the ark, Name, and saving action.", "positions": [{"id": "11:41/q28/p1", "position": "The ark figures reliance on God or the Sharia as a means of rescue from spiritual danger.", "reasons": "Al-Qushayrī stresses God's name and favor over schemes; al-Rāzī likens a knowledge seeker to a vessel of reflection amid waves of error. Al-Burṣawī says the Sharia's ark saves from self and world only through commanded obedience, not imitation or instinct."}, {"id": "11:41/q28/p2", "position": "God's greatest Name is the fully realized human knower through whom law enters and stands in the material world.", "reasons": "Al-Qāshānī includes prophets, imams and scholars; he reads forgiveness as removal of dark bodily traits and mercy as knowledge and unveiling that save from drowning."}, {"id": "11:41/q28/p3", "position": "God forgives those saved by boarding and has mercy on those who board in obedience to the command.", "reasons": "Al-Burṣawī contrasts the latter with instinctive boarding; he cites hypocrites and Iblis as examples of ineffective imitation."}]}
{"id": "11:41/q29", "question": "How does this verse relate to other guidance about travel and safety?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "11:41/q29/p1", "position": "It pairs naming God at departure with thanksgiving and prayer on reaching safety.", "reasons": "Ibn Kathīr compares 23:28–29 and 43:12–14 and recommends naming God on a ship or animal; al-Qurṭubī and Ibn Kathīr connect the protection formula with 39:67."}, {"id": "11:41/q29/p2", "position": "The ship's bearing of passengers explains the choice of ark wording here.", "reasons": "Iṣlāḥī contrasts the carrying image in Hūd with al-Muʾminūn, where sulūk describes entry instead."}, {"id": "11:41/q29/p3", "position": "Noah's naming God is the first such invocation reported of a person in revealed scripture

{"id": "11:41/q30", "question": "What do the neighboring flood descriptions add?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "11:41/q30/p1", "position": "The ark's sailing through mountain-like waves completes the mention of its movement and shows the scale of rescue.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr calls the description parenthetical; al-Biqāʿī says the waves' image conveys height, bulk, and accumulation. {"id": "11:41/q31", "question": "How is the following clause “and it sailed with them” parsed?", "turns_on": "Whether the following clause is independent or circumstantial and where its prepositional phrase attaches.", "positions": [{"id": "11:41/q31/p1", "position": "It is an independent or circumstantial clause describing the ship's movement after the invocation.", "reasons": "Al-Samīn reports attachment to a hidden pronoun in bismillāh or to an omitted contextual element; al-Zamakhsharī supplies their embarking while saying bismillāh."}, {"id": "11:41/q31/p2", "position": "Bihim attaches directly to “it sailed.”", "reasons": "Al-Samīn gives the direct grammatical attachment; al-Zamakhsharī glosses it as their being aboard."}, {"id": "11:41/q31/p3", "position": "Bihim attaches to an omitted element meaning the vessel carried them.", "reasons": "Al-Samīn records the alternative."}]}
{"id": "11:41/q32", "question": "What background reports describe Noah before and while making the ark?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "11:41/q32/p1", "position": "Noah endured beatings and persisted in preaching while seeking his people's pardon.", "reasons": "Mujāhid and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr report a beating and his “forgive my people” prayer; Ibn ʿAbbās gives felt wrapping, renewed preaching, and another attack. Al-Ḥasan says he preached day and night, openly and secretly, for 950 years (29:14), and prayed for forgiveness."}, {"id": "11:41/q32/p2", "position": "After Noah prayed for guidance or patience, God said no more would believe and ordered him not to grieve.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās's report links this to 11:36."}, {"id": "11:41/q32/p3", "position": "Noah lived in Damascus and built the ark from Lebanese wood near the sanctuary.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās locates the construction between Zamzam, the Black Stone and the Station."}]}
{"id": "11:41/q33", "question": "What ancillary words and reports near this verse are explained?", "turns_on": "These notes explain adjacent wording or cited material rather than a single word of 11:41.", "positions": [{"id": "11:41/q33/p1", "position": "The water's subsiding means decreasing; related neighboring verbs describe absorbing and ceasing.", "reasons": "Mujāhid glosses subsiding as decreasing; Abū Ḥayyān says ghāḍa is intransitive or transitive, iqlaʿ means ceasing as with rain or fever, and al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ give kasra or fatḥa on the lām of balaʿa, relating bālūʿa to water absorption."}, {"id": "11:41/q33/p2", "position": "Labīd's quoted ḥarsan means a long duration.", "reasons": "Abū ʿUbayda explains this accompanying poetic word."}, {"id": "11:41/q33/p3", "position": "The reading of “my son” varies in the neighboring verse.", "reasons": "Al-Jishumī says Ḥafṣ opens the yāʾ throughout the Qur'an, while others use kasra except Ibn Kathīr's Luqmān report; kasra transfers the elided hamzat al-waṣl vowel, while fatḥa is lighter."}, {"id": "11:41/q33/p4", "position": "Divine “eyes” in the related ark passages can mean sight or God's signs.", "reasons": "Al-Suyūṭī reports both a literal sight reading and Ibn al-Labbān's signs reading, comparing 27:13, 6:104, 76:24, and 20:38."}]}
{"id": "11:41/q34", "question": "What historical use of the ark phrase is reported?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "11:41/q34/p1", "position": "The phrase in Hūd's sūra succeeded an earlier prophetic document opening “In Your name, O God.”", "reasons": "Al-Shaʿbī reports that the Prophet wrote four documents, the first beginning with that formula, before Hūd was revealed."}]}
{"id": "11:53/q01", "question": "How is this reply introduced after Hūd's appeal?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "11:53/q01/p1", "position": "It is the people's direct answer to Hūd's call and counsel.", "reasons": "Bursevī says قالوا starts a new answer to an implied question about their response after his commands and prohibitions. Ibn ʿĀshūr says the absence of a conjunction marks dialogue responding to an invitation. Biqāʿī says Hūd's exceptionally clear counsel and signs drew only rejection."}]}

{"id": "11:53/q03", "question": "What does bayyina mean here?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "11:53/q03/p1", "position": "A clear proof or sign establishing the truth of Hūd's claim and distinguishing truth from falsehood.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī derives the name from its making truth distinct from falsehood. Biqāʿī connects it to bayān, which separates and clarifies a meaning in the mind. Abū Ḥayyān calls it an argument for the truth of Hūd's claim; Bḍ, reported by Study Quran, says it verifies his being God's prophet. The other glosses call it clear explanation, proof, argument, or miracle."}]}
{"id": "11:53/q04", "question": "How do interpreters understand the claim that Hūd brought no proof?", "turns_on": "Whether 'no proof' states what the people demanded or accurately describes the evidence Hūd had actually shown.", "positions": [{"id": "11:53/q04/p1", "position": "The people assert that Hūd supplied no evidence adequate to establish his divine mission.", "reasons": "Muqātil, al-Ṭabarī and others explain the claim as refusing to concede his truthful call to worship God alone and his prophethood. Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says they treat the call as unsupported and thus unworthy of heed. Ibn ʿAṭiyya says they deny that his miracles count as signs; his analogy is Quraysh's dismissal of the Quran as magic or poetry."}, {"id": "11:53/q04/p2", "position": "They demanded a palpable miracle or signs matching their own demands.", "reasons": "Iṣlāḥī says they required a palpable miracle before accepting Hūd or abandoning their deities. Ibn ʿĀshūr says Hūd's actual signs failed to meet their demands; their claim is presented as a reason to keep the gods, though this is no logical inference from seeing no sign."}, {"id": "11:53/q04/p3", "position": "Their denial was false: Hūd had brought real signs and miracles.", "reasons": "Al-Wāḥidī calls it slander and transgression. Al-Zamakhsharī, al-Nasafī, al-Bursawī and Biqāʿī compare Quraysh's sign demands despite the Prophet's signs; Biqāʿī cites 13:7. Al-Rāzī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya, Abū Ḥayyān and al-Ālūsī affirm Hūd's miracles. Ibn ʿĀshūr and Kuranyolu cite 11:59 while saying no particular miracle is identified; Ibn ʿĀshūr tentatively suggests a prediction of exceptional abundance and continuous fertility, and also mentions 41:15. Al-Kuranyolu adds rational proofs. Bḍ, as reported by Study Quran, attributes the failure to see proofs to obstinacy."}]}
{"id": "11:53/q05", "question": "Why did they deny or fail to recognize Hūd's evidence?", "turns_on": "The notes attribute the denial variously to willful resistance, poor attention, learned assumptions, or inward veiling.", "positions": [{"id": "11:53/q05/p1", "position": "Deliberate obstinacy, slander, and refusal made them deny clear signs.", "reasons": "Al-Wāḥidī calls the claim slander and refusal to accept evidence; al-Bayḍāwī calls it extreme obstinacy. Biqāʿī says they resisted clear reason and transmitted proof and that their emphatic defiance belies sincere uncertainty. Al-Bursawī and Bḍ, reported in Study Quran, likewise stress obstinate rejection; Ibn ʿĀshūr calls the denial slander."}, {"id": "11:53/q05/p2", "position": "Blindness to truth and failure to examine the signs led them to misjudge them.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls their failure blindness. Abū Ḥayyān reports blindness and neglect of consideration as an explanation. Al-Ālūsī offers blindness and inattention as an alternative to stubborn resistance."}, {"id": "11:53/q05/p3", "position": "Imitation, doubt, false premises, and hostility toward the messenger obstructed reflection.", "reasons": "Al-Jishumī names doubts, imitation of leaders, and false premises. Al-Ṭabrisī adds imitation of ancestors, rejection of the bearer without examining evidence, and suspicion about validity. Biqāʿī adds suppression of doubt, accusing the source, and envy; he says doubt underlies these causes."}, {"id": "11:53/q05/p4", "position": "Natural veils blinded their inner sight to the demonstration.", "reasons": "Al-Qāshānī gives an inward account of why they could not grasp the proof."}]}

{"id": "11:53/q08", "question": "Why did they worship idols?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "11:53/q08/p1", "position": "They sought nearness to God, expected worldly favor, or fashioned divine likenesses under anthropomorphic ideas.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabrisī gives these alternatives: presumed intercession, Satan's promise of worldly benefit, and images shaped by a conceived divine form."}]}
{"id": "11:53/q09", "question": "What do they mean by refusing to leave their gods, and how sound is their reason?", "turns_on": "Whether lack of a newly accepted sign justifies continued idol worship when reason already distinguishes God from powerless idols.", "positions": [{"id": "11:53/q09/p1", "position": "They will keep worshipping the idols and will not abandon them merely on Hūd's word.", "reasons": "Muqātil and al-Jishumī say they reject his order to leave worship they regard as permissible. Ibn ʿAṭiyya says they consider his statement unsupported by a sign; al-Ālūsī calls it a bare assertion in their view. Ibn ʿĀshūr says they present unmet sign demands as a reason, though it does not logically follow. Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the refusal answers one part of Hūd's appeal."}, {"id": "11:53/q09/p2", "position": "Reason itself requires leaving powerless idols, regardless of Hūd's personal assertion.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī argues that the people already admit only God brings benefit and harm while idols bring neither, making their stated reasoning poor."}]}
{"id": "11:53/q10", "question": "Why is the nūn absent from tārikī?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "11:53/q10/p1", "position": "The active participle is annexed to ālihatinā, so its final nūn is dropped.", "reasons": "Al-Bursawī explains the omission by the iḍāfa construction."}]}
{"id": "11:53/q11", "question": "What does ʿan qawlik mean and how is it constructed?", "turns_on": "Whether ʿan is circumstantial or causal, and whether a departure expression is omitted or understood through semantic inclusion.", "positions": [{"id": "11:53/q11/p1", "position": "It is a circumstantial phrase tied to the pronoun in tārikī: they would leave their gods while departing from Hūd's saying.", "reasons": "Al-Zamakhsharī, as reported by Abū Ḥayyān, supplies the circumstantial analysis; al-Nasafī, al-Samīn and al-Bursawī follow it. Al-Bayḍāwī describes their state in refusing. Al-Samīn explicitly prefers it over causal attachment; al-Bursawī says this construction makes Hūd's word the effective cause more strongly than bi or li. Al-Ālūsī reports a variant in which 'departing' means turning away from the word, restricting the negation and answering Hūd's 11:52 injunction not to turn away."}, {"id": "11:53/q11/p2", "position": "ʿAn marks cause and attaches to 'leaving': Hūd's word will not induce them to abandon their gods.", "reasons": "Al-Wāḥidī and Ibn al-Jawzī say ʿan and bāʾ can interchange; al-Wāḥidī cites 7:187 and 25:59, and Ibn al-Jawzī's Nuzha cites 53:3. Al-Ṭabrisī reports the same replacement. Ibn ʿAṭiyya, reported by Abū Ḥayyān and al-Samīn, makes it causal; 9:114 is cited. Al-Burhān and al-Itqān use Abraham's prayer after a promise as a parallel, with al-Burhān also comparing Lot's people's reported words. Al-Bursawī reports al-Saʿdī al-Muftī's بسبب analysis and 9:114. Al-Ālūsī and Ibn ʿĀshūr take causal ʿan; Ibn ʿĀshūr connects its basic departure sense to causal usage and cites 18:82."}, {"id": "11:53/q11/p3", "position": "An omitted circumstantial expression of departing and acting on Hūd's word mediates the phrase.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī reports careful grammarians attaching the phrase to an omitted state rather than directly to 'leaving.' He explains that departure from and return to water became metaphors for managing affairs, cites a verse about sound judgment, and says Arabic may omit 'returning' because departure implies it. On this reading negation covers both actions: they neither leave their gods nor act on Hūd's word. Abū Zakariyyā, reported by Ibn al-Jawzī, says ʿan fundamentally signifies passing beyond, illustrated by speech reaching a listener and turning from Zayd; he also says it is a preposition except after min, where it becomes a noun because a preposition cannot govern another."}, {"id": "11:53/q11/p4", "position": "The construction may use semantic inclusion rather than an omitted complement.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī reports this analysis from some interpreters and says al-Zamakhsharī's wording appears to support it, as al-Kashf explains."}]}
{"id": "11:53/q12", "question": "Why does the second refusal use waw rather than causal fa?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "11:53/q12/p1", "position": "Waw coordinates the refusal without making the earlier no-proof claim its formal cause.", "reasons": "Biqāʿī notes that fa would make the first statement the cause of the second."}]}
{"id": "11:53/q13", "question": "What does their refusal to believe Hūd cover?", "turns_on": "Whether the rejected object is his mission, truth generally, or all of his words and acts.", "positions": [{"id": "11:53/q13/p1", "position": "They will not affirm Hūd's prophethood, message, or call to worship God alone.", "reasons": "Muqātil and al-Ṭabarī specify his messengerhood. {"id": "11:53/q22", "question": "Who were ʿĀd, and what background and fate frame their reply?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "11:53/q22/p1", "position": "They were an ancient, powerful Arab people who turned to idolatry, rejected their kinsman Hūd, and were destroyed by wind while Hūd and believers were saved.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says their history survives in unreliable tales and the extant Torah omits them; the Quran places them after Noah in al-Aḥqāf, perhaps as 'first ʿĀd' implying a second.
